title: True Colors
html:
True Colors

Quest Type

Companion

Character

Zhezhi

Requirements

Reach Union Level 22
Complete Event Main Quest Wish Upon the Moon I: Cry of the Soul in By Moon's Grace: Tale of Moontree Lodge

Description

What does it really mean to create? Will this artist find the courage to confront her past mistakes as she gets caught up again in past accusations? Will she be able to reconnect with her emotions and talents, and continue to breathe new life into her paintings?

Gameplay Notes[]

  • Completing the "Inspect the object" step awards the item Serenity of Xiehua Village.
  • Completing the "Defeat the Tacet Discords (0/4)" step in the Ashened Gallery awards the Exploration: Huanglong trophy Colors Revived.
  • Completing the quest awards the Moments with You trophy Preserve the True Colors.

Dialogue[]

Quest Description
On the way to the Pioneer Association for new tasks, you received a sudden call from Zhezhi, saying that she was summoned to appear at a dispute hearing...
What is the purpose of this hearing, and what's the story behind it? Caught up in a struggle of consciousness, will this artist being tried find the courage to reconnect with her emotions and talents, and continue to breathe new life into her paintings?
(Head to the Pioneer Association)
(If Rover met Zhezhi during the Moon-Chasing Festival, talk to Maqi)
Maqi: The client has received the mine investigation report. We can wrap up this case. Thank you once again for your contribution!
Maqi: But before you go, we have a art project that may be right for you if you're interested.
Maqi: The client seeks an artist to capture a few scenic spots, both photos and paintings will do.
Landscape painting... reminds me of someone.
Rover: I met a painter called Zhezhi during the Moon-Chasing Festival. We had a blast at the festival.
Rover: The first time I saw her, she was busy sketching scenery, so absorbed in her work that her mind was still on it when we talked.
I remember doing landscape paintings with Zhezhi.
Rover: At the Moon-Chasing Festival, we worked together on a painting commission. Her brushwork was so exquisite and expressive.
Maqi: Oh, right! She helped out at the fan drawing stall during the festival. Her artwork was so popular, I couldn't get one myself.
Maqi: Now that you mention it, she seems perfect for this job! If she takes it, the client will be very pleased.
Maqi: Thanks for bringing this up! We will make sure to contact her.
Zhezhi (Contacting): (‍RoverThe player's chosen name for Rover‍), it's almost time for the dispute hearing.
Zhezhi (Contacting): I... I still hope you'll come with me.
Zhezhi (Contacting): I don't mean to burden you, but if you'd like to come, please meet me at the Public Security Bureau entrance.
Zhezhi: I didn't expect such a big crowd at the hearing...
Zhezhi: Hmm... S-should I take the stand myself? What do you think, little kitty?
Zhezhi: Ah, maybe we can do a little show of... um... paws. Raise your left paw if you think I should testify, or your right paw if...
Zhezhi: W-wait! You raised your left paw before I even finished my sentence... No, that doesn't count. Let's try again.
Zhezhi: Okay, if you raise your right paw, I'll... let someone else handle it.
Zhezhi: Hmm... right paw, huh? Well... I did actually want to tell everyone the truth myself. Let's give this another shot.
Juyao: Ms. Zhezhi, the hearing is about to start. If you would, please join us.
Zhezhi: Now? Y-yes, Madam Juyao! I... I'll be there in a minute!
Hi, Zhezhi. I've made it.
Zhezhi: (‍RoverThe player's chosen name for Rover‍), oh, you're here! It's... it's really nice to see you! And... I appreciate you coming.
Zhezhi: I just handed over all the evidence we gathered from Mingyan's studio and the Exile's camp to the Patrollers.
Zhezhi: Now the Shanyun Art Exchange can't deny the fact they were producing and trading art forgeries.
Zhezhi: But... there is one more thing. The Patroller said we still need someone to testify in the hearing.
Do you want me to testify?
Zhezhi: You're really kind, but... um, I'll be fine to do this myself. You've already helped me so much, even just having you here is a huge relief.
Zhezhi: Some things, I've got to face on my own.
Zhezhi: That said... I, uh, didn't... didn't expect there would be so many spectators coming to watch...
Zhezhi: If I get nervous and mess up any details, could you please help to remind me?
No problem.
Zhezhi: Thank you! Having you here helps, more than you know.
Zhezhi: It's about time. We should probably go in, huh?
You can do this. I believe in you.
Zhezhi: Eh? B-but... I've... I've never spoken in front of so many people before...
Zhezhi: H-how about... you do the talking, and, um, I'll add details... if, if I have to?
You know this case better than I do.
Actually, I kind of forgot the details...
Rover: We wouldn't want my lack of artistic expertise to give the Shanyun Art Exchange a chance to turn the hearing against us.
Zhezhi: You're right... Then... I'll... I'll do it myself...
Relax, I'll be here if you need me.
Rover: Don't worry, I've got your back. Just remember, you're the only one who can lay out the truth—the whole truth— for everyone to see.
Zhezhi: ...You're right.
Zhezhi: I was the one who chose to uncover the truth behind this case. I can't back down now, not when it matters most.
Zhezhi: I'll give it my all, I promise. Let's go.
(Enter the Public Security Bureau with Zhezhi)
Juyao: With both parties present, this hearing is now in session. Let us begin.
Juyao: First, a brief overview of the case before us.
Juyao: Ms. Zhezhi alleges that the guilty party, Mingyan, implicated in the Tacet Discord Assault, was coerced into committing art fraud under duress.
Juyao: Therefore, her mental state was adversely affected, which led to her committing actions contrary to her will.
Juyao: Today, based on new evidence provided by Ms. Zhezhi and the result of this hearing, we will determine whether to revisit Mingyan's charges and consider if the Shanyun Art Exchange is indeed guilty of selling illegal art forgeries.
Baici: What?! With all due respect, this doesn't match what we discussed before!
Juyao: Mr. Baici, I remind you that any evidence or arguments presented before and during the hearing are valid.
Juyao: If you would like to add further information, you are welcome to do so at any point.
Juyao: Now, without further ado, either party may begin their opening statement.
Zhezhi: Madam Juyao, th-the situation is...
Baici: Madam Juyao, as the head of the Shanyun Art Exchange, I, Baici, must clear our name and seek justice here today.
Baici: There are two points I'd like to address. Firstly, the authenticity of our artworks remains unimpeachable. Secondly, Mingyan's provocative creations stem solely from her own greed and vanity. She alone should bear responsibility for the assault.
Baici: Throughout my tenure at the Art Exchange, our foremost principle has been that of integrity, a well known fact. And yet...
Baici: Integrity in business is not enough to stave off discord.
Baici: We are aware of certain painters, rejected by the Art Exchange, nursing grudges, and resorting to threats...
Baici: They bombarded us with spite and slander, causing a public uproar simply because they didn't get what they wanted.
Baici: Should the public be swayed by these slanderous insinuations, that paint us as wicked fraudsters, then I'm afraid justice will never be served!
Juyao: Please control yourself, Mr. Baici.
Baici: Forgive me, Madam, but if this injustice persists, I will have no choice but to sue them for harming the Shanyun Art Exchange's reputation. They have damaged the trust we built with our clients!
Baici: I demand they compensate us for our losses and issue a public apology!
Baici: Such disgraceful behavior will not diminish us! Our principles will not waver, and we will protect the Shanyun Art Exchange from any ill intent!
He's actually blaming the victim now...
He's trying to change the topic...
Zhezhi: ...
Yan: I've bought paintings from Shanyun Art Exchange before. They were good quality, and their service was decent. Hard to believe they'd be involved in something like this...
Woyun: The honest always get the short end of the stick... But who's Mingyan? A painter? Never heard of them...
Qianzhang: Tsk, must be some nobody trying to get attention using the Shanyun's name.
Fuqing: Why is the Art Exchange always in the middle of some controversy?
Juyao: Order! Order!
Juyao: You may continue your statement.
Zhezhi: I...
Zhezhi: ...
Rover: Madam, allow us to present our account of the events.
Rover: This all really began three days ago.
Rover: I was entrusted to investigate a certain "Arcane Artist" in the Tiger's Maw.
Gupan: Hey, Rover! Took you long enough to get here!
So you were the one who ordered this task.
Gupan: Things are getting awfully strange around the mine lately. Figured you're just the one to untangle this mess.
Gupan: With your knack for solving mysteries, you'll figure this out in no time!
What happened?
Gupan: I don't know if you've ever heard of it, but there's a special folktale in Jinzhou...
Gupan: Word has it, there's this mysterious Arcane Artist whose paintings come to life as they paint, as if each brushstroke has a life of its own.
Gupan: Once their canvas dries, whatever they've painted leaps right off the page. Mythical creatures, the whole shebang—all real as day!
Gupan: The thing is, anyone who might've seen these paintings? Well, they vanish into thin air...
What does the mine have to do with all of this?
Sounds like a Forte to me.
Gupan: I've never heard of such unique Forte.
Gupan: Lately, I've been receiving reports about eerie monsters wandering the mine at midnight. Some witnesses even ran into them more than once!
Gupan: These monsters, they look like paintings from a distance. But approach them and they're as docile as can be.
Gupan: Reading these reports, I couldn't shake the tale of the Arcane Artist from my mind.
Gupan: Sure, some say it's just a prank or some new Tacet Discord variant...
Gupan: But with rumors swirling, folks are getting jittery. Can't let things escalate. That's why I reached out to you.
Let me take it from here.
Gupan: Great! Counting on you to crack this case wide open.
Good pay, good service.
Gupan: Deal! I'll pay whatever it takes to keep the goosebumps coming. I can't wait for you to uncover the truth!
Gupan: Oh, and you might want to chat up the witnesses. Got their names right here for you.
(Talk to Huaijin)
Huaijin: That's it for today. Time for a break! Oh, hey there. Need something?
Tell me about the recent event at the mine.
Huaijin: You've come to the right guy. I was actually the first to see those weird things.
Huaijin: I was playing chess with the old miners until midnight, then headed home alone. On my way back, I heard these strange moans, like some kind of monster was out there.
Huaijin: At first, I thought they were Tacet Discords and I was ready to bolt. But then I realized they were different. These monsters... they were being drawn to something.
Huaijin: Curiosity got the better of me, so I took a step closer...
Huaijin: ...And saw that they had these strange features. Gleaming eyes, gnarled horns, and dark green bodies covered in slimy liquid...
Could it be a new variant of TD?
Huaijin: Hmm, maybe... But unlike Tacet Discords, they didn't attack me.
Could it be a prank?
Huaijin: No way... Those monsters showed up in an empty field at midnight, so there was no one around to prank. Besides, what's the point of tricks if there's no one to see them?
Could it be related to the Arcane Artist?
Huaijin: Do you think they're related? Did Gupan tell you about that old folktale?
Huaijin: You know, I did see some people standing nearby. Just some shadows, really, 'cause it was so dim.
Huaijin: The light was flickering in the wind, so I couldn't make out their faces. But I knew something was weird with the scrolls they had in their hands. Every time they moved, more monsters appeared.
Huaijin: Later, I told everyone about it, and Gupan was there. She freaked out, saying it was just like the tale of the Arcane Artist.
They? There was more than one person on the scene that night?
Huaijin: I'm not sure... but I overheard them talking. No, actually, "arguing" would be more accurate.
Huaijin: Anyway, I got worried those monsters might attack me, so I bolted and didn't catch what they were arguing about...
Do you remember where you saw them?
Huaijin: I do remember... Wait, you're not seriously thinking of going there, are you? Whatever those monsters are, they're unidentified and dangerous. If you have to go, be really careful, alright?
(Talk to Jifeng)
Jifeng: Uh... You don't look like you work at the mine. Can I help you with something?
Tell me about the recent event at the mine.
Jifeng: Oh yes, that strange event. It's the talk of the town right now.
Jifeng: I've conducted several investigations and found that those monsters tend to appear around midnight. Their locations seem random, though.
Jifeng: Fortunately, they haven't caused much harm. I think it's because they always show up and vanish in the dead of night.
Jifeng: If you ask me, these monsters are a new type of Tacet Discord. Since they're unrecorded, our Terminal can't trigger an alarm when they're nearby.
Jifeng: For safety reasons, we have increased our patrols around the mine.
Did you notice anything else unusual?
Jifeng: Anything else unusual? Hmm... Yes there was one thing.
Could it be related to the Arcane Artist?
Jifeng: Do you mean the mysterious painter who can bring fantastical creatures to life? That could explain it, but a Forte tied to painting is rare.
Jifeng: Aside from the blurred silhouettes I saw that night, I remember hearing voices—like people talking.
Jifeng: The voices came from where those silhouettes were, but they sounded like... vague muttering.
Jifeng: Thinking about it now, if it was a human voice, how could someone get so close to those monsters without crying out for help?
I see. Thank you for the information.
(Approach the Resonance Nexus)
Injured Miner: That's so scary...
Timid Miner: It's just a prank, I bet.
(Optional - Inquire with the two miners in front of the Resonance Nexus)
Injured Miner: You see my arm here? The monsters mauled me.
Injured Miner: I heard laughter, voices with them. Will there be half-human Tacet Discords? Like... hybrids?
Timid Miner: Stop. You're giving me the chills...
Injured Miner: Stop being so paranoid. Remember last time, when that guy was collecting laundry on a skateboard and you thought it was a ghost? You need to calm down.
(Approach the exit to the Tiger's Maw Mine)
Woman: No. The paintings came first, then the monsters and humans followed.
Man on the right: No. The humans came first, then the monsters and paintings followed.
Man on the left: No. The monsters ARE the humans.
(Head to the designated location)
Rover: I've gathered enough information. It's time to check the scene where those monsters were spotted.
(Head to the designated location)
Rover: There's... something ahead...
Rover: That figure... that paintbrush... Could it be...
(Head to the designated location)
Rover: Nothing here. That's odd... Did I just imagine that?
Zhezhi...?
Zhezhi: R-rover? You're here...
Zhezhi: Sorry, did I scare you just now?
I'm fine. Why are you here?
Zhezhi: ...F-finding inspiration.
Zhezhi: The night... often sparks my creativity...
...Don't tell me you are actually the Arcane Artist.
Zhezhi: Of course not!
Zhezhi: I... I heard about the tale of the Arcane Artist and hoped to find out who they are...
Zhezhi: Sorry I lied to you, I just... didn't want to drag anyone else into this...
You too? Why are you investigating this?
Are you also a ghost story enthusiast?
Zhezhi: N-no, I'm not into ghost stories.
Zhezhi: Bringing painted creatures to life, making fantasies real—it sounds like a fairy tale, but when the Arcane Artist first caught people's attention in Jinzhou years ago, it was more than just a tale.
Zhezhi: Now this story is making the rounds again. Most don't see the dangers it holds. As someone who feels the threat, I... I want to uncover the truth before it's too late.
The Arcane Artist showed up before?
Zhezhi: Yes, there was once an artist who could create paintings that felt so real, you could almost step into them...
Zhezhi: But these paintings, they strayed from the artist's original intentions and... caused a lot of trouble.
Zhezhi: I don't know who's behind these latest events, but if it's really the Arcane Artist... their paintings will bring nothing but trouble. T-that's why I... I have to stop them, to prevent the past from repeating itself...
Zhezhi: Unfortunately, I'm... not very good at investigating, so I haven't found any major clues yet.
Zhezhi: I'm here for the Arcane Artist, but also hoping to meet an old acquaintance. Maybe he knows what happened in the mine...
I'll go with you. It's linked to the case I'm investigating.
Zhezhi: Is that so? O-ok.
(Head to the designated location)
Shilang: Hey, Zhezhi! Long time no see! You need more pigments already?
Zhezhi: N-no, not yet...
Shilang: And this must be the Rover! Nice to meet you. Heard a lot about you. Didn't realize you and Zhezhi knew each other.
We met during the Moon-Chasing Festival.
Zhezhi: But I've never had the chance to introduce myself properly...
Shilang: Great moment for it! Here's the thing, Rover. I can't say I know Zhezhi very well, but I do know she's got this quirk where her courage tends to crumble right when it's crunchtime.
Shilang: So, when it comes to introducing herself to you, I'd bet money on it she's been mentally rehearsing it for forever before she got the guts to take action.
Zhezhi: No, it's not like that!
Shilang: Zhezhi, you can't keep avoiding things! You've got to take action, or you'll never get what you want! You only live once, right?!
That does make sense.
Well, that's a bit too much...
Zhezhi: Yes... Mr. Shilang is right. Rover, I've actually been meaning to tell you something.
Zhezhi: Hello, my name is Zhezhi. We have met before, but I'd like to make this a formal request. I would really like for us to become friends!
Rover: Of course, I'd be happy to.
Shilang: Hello? Zhezhi?
Shilang: Hey, what are you waiting for?
Zhezhi: Eh? I... um... Okay! I can do this!
Zhezhi: Um... Rober...
 ?
Shilang: (That was a pretty obvious slip of the tongue...)
Zhezhi: Ahem! Nice to meet you, my name is Zhezhi. I'm... a painter. I take art commissions and strive to create beautiful paintings.
Zhezhi: I... I'm not being very articulate... b-but I hope we can be friends!
Hello, I'm (‍RoverThe player's chosen name for Rover‍).
We're already friends.
Shilang: Haha, how sweet! I must say, I've never seen Zhezhi this nervous since she first became one of my cherished patrons.
Zhezhi: W-wait, Mr. Shilang! We're actually here today to talk about the tale of the Arcane Artist.
Shilang: Oh, I know the tale, but I've never come across this mystical maestro myself.
Shilang: If such an artist truly existed, I'd be the first to know, without a doubt!
What makes you say that?
Shilang: I supply ore to pigment manufacturers, and sometimes serve as their sales proxy, so most painters in Jinzhou come to my shop to buy pigments.
Anything suspicious about the pigment buyers?
Shilang: Hmm... pigments aren't flying off the shelves these days. Just a few regulars, you know?
Shilang: Oh... but those ore buyers from a while back, they seemed a bit suspicious.
Shilang: They bought heaps of leftover ore—the cheapest type—and told me not to let anyone know they got the ore here.
Shilang: People don't usually buy that stuff. Oh wait, Zhezhi, didn't you buy some once? A long time ago, right?
Shilang: I remember you saying you couldn't afford the fancy pigments, so you made your own. That stuck with me.
Shilang: So when those guys asked for leftovers, I paid extra attention.
Zhezhi: Are you sure you can tell us this? I thought they asked you to keep it a secret...
Shilang: Pft, they turned out to be thieves who stole from me during the night! When I found out, I reported the theft to the Patrollers and that was the end of it.
Shilang: Thieves don't deserve my business or respect.
May I have a look at your transaction record?
Shilang: Of course. Help yourself.

Zhezhi: If this is the situation...
Chixia: Hmm? (‍RoverThe player's chosen name for Rover‍)? Hey! (‍RoverThe player's chosen name for Rover‍)!
Chixia: What brings you here? It's been ages since we last met! The Patrol Station's been pretty busy lately, so I haven't had the time to catch up with you.
Chixia: And Zhezhi's here too! Hiya! Do you remember me? We met at the Moon-Chasing Festival.
Chixia: Oh? Are you alright? You don't look well... Do you need help?
Zhezhi: H-hello... No, it's not... uh... no, thank you...
Chixia: The painting we had you do for us during the festival is awesome! Everyone loves it, so we put it up on the wall!
Zhezhi: Really? Hehe, I'm glad you all like it...
Chixia: We'd also like to invite you to our station, so we can formally thank you in person!
Chixia: Wait, how bout' coming to the station with me today? Are you heading back to the city?
Zhezhi: Uh... but we're still investig— I... O-okay.
Are you sure we can go now?
Chixia: Oh, is this not a good time?
Wait, we have a case to investigate.
Chixia: Investigate? About what? A new case?
Yes, about the Arcane Artist tale.
Chixia: Oh, I get it! In that case, it's probably not the best time for a get-together.
Zhezhi: Sorry...
Chixia: That's okay! Just tell me if you need any help!
Thanks. But why are you here, Chixia?
Chixia: I'm here to support the Patrollers. There was an assault near the mine recently, and they're short on people to investigate.
Chixia: What's odd is those monsters haven't caused any more trouble since we got here. Right now, we're talking to witnesses and trying to figure out what triggered the incident.
Zhezhi: Did something just happen over there...
Chixia: Don't tell me it's a Tacet Discord... Hold on, just got a message... Seems like they really are stirring up trouble again. Sorry, but I gotta go check this out!
We'll go with you.
Zhezhi: S-should we go as well?
Why not? Maybe we'll find some clues useful to our case.
Zhezhi: You could be right, but there's one other thing...
Zhezhi: After (‍RoverThe player's chosen name for Rover‍) and I bumped into each other, we decided to investigate the surroundings and follow Patroller Chixia to the scene of the incident.
Zhezhi: It was there we learned about the details of Mingyan's offense and the truth behind the tale of the Arcane Artist.
Rover: (Once Zhezhi has the paintbrush in her hand, she begins to speak calmly.)
Rover: (She'll be fine making the statement on her own now.)
(Defeat the TDs)
Zhezhi seems to be struggling to tell what she couldn't express earlier, but eventually stays silent.
Zhezhi: Phew... Sorry to trouble you, (‍RoverThe player's chosen name for Rover‍).
Why are you apologizing all of a sudden?
Don't worry about it.
Zhezhi: Thanks... Uh, wait, I haven't said why.
Zhezhi: What I'm trying to say is...
Zhezhi: If I had been clearer, you wouldn't have had to explain things to Chixia for me.
Zhezhi: She's really nice. It's just... we're not that close, and I'm not sure how to respond to how friendly she is... I didn't want to be rude, so I... I couldn't bring myself to turn her down.
It's okay. I got you.
Her friendliness is infectious.
Zhezhi: I'll do my best not to trouble you and express my feelings properly next time...
I'm sure you will.
No trouble at all.
Zhezhi: Thank you...
Then both of you decide to ask people around about the situation.
(Approach the crowd)
Contemplating Onlooker: Wasn't someone standing there with the painter before it happened?
(Optional - Listen in on the miner and worker)
Contemplating Onlooker: Wasn't someone standing there with the painter before it happened?
Chatting Onlooker: Really? Should we go tell the Patrollers about it?
Contemplating Onlooker: Maybe, but I don't even remember what that person looked like...
Chatting Onlooker: Was that her partner in crime, maybe?
Contemplating Onlooker: They were arguing over something... The painter looked ready to snap...
Chatting Onlooker: That sounds concerning. We should tell the Patrollers.
Contemplating Onlooker: Yeah, let's go.
(Talk to Chixia)
Chixia: Thanks for your help, (‍RoverThe player's chosen name for Rover‍)! We caught the culprit before anything worse could happen... We were lucky to have you here!
What was the cause of the incident?
Researcher: According to the preliminary examination, we suspect that these Tacet Discords were agitated by the Frequency Fluctuations from a scroll painting found at the scene.
Researcher: The energy remaining in the painting was generated by its creator's Forte nearly overclocking.
Researcher: But rest assured, we've calmed her down and contained the energy.
So she is the Arcane Artist.
It's a Forte. Just as I suspected...
Researcher: The painting needs to be thoroughly examined to identify its connection with the monsters and eliminate any potential risk it still poses.
